records.title: Diverse Evidence, Better Forecasts: Multi-Agent Deliberation Under Information Asymmetry
records.mechanism: Public/private evidence partition, BM25-based routing, iterative deliberation and confidence aggregation alter information diversity.
records.boundary: Information partition is already proposed. Its linear-error correlation analysis requires assumptions; it does not prove arbitrary LLM private errors independent. It does not by itself establish graph-credit revalidation utility.
records.implication_for_mab2: Shared input redundancy is an environment mechanism worth measuring, but evidence partition is not a new MAB2 algorithm. Any future common/private condition must give every baseline identical information and charge retrieval/routing cost.

records.title: Learning Who Talks to Whom: Role-Aware Communication Topology Scheduling for Efficient LLM Multi-Agent Collaboration
records.mechanism: Role-conditioned relational attention and a topology-aware value mixer train adaptive communication schedules.
records.boundary: Its information-gain quantity is a task-accuracy heuristic with an exploration term, not a mutual-information estimator or a significance test. The audited excerpts do not establish private evidence partition.
records.implication_for_mab2: Learned graph-aware scheduling is occupied prior work. MAB2 must isolate purchased revalidation feedback under fixed models, not relabel a topology-conditioned predictor as the contribution.

records.title: Multi-Fidelity Best-Arm Identification
records.mechanism: IISE chooses among costly accurate observations and cheaper biased fidelities, assuming known maximum fidelity biases.
records.implication_for_mab2: A partial receiver rollout can be a paid screening feature, but its unknown relation to final quality is not a known-bias fidelity. No IISE guarantee transfers without verifying the required bounds.

records.relationship: Recheck of existing historical cats entry; not a newly discovered paper or independent reproduction
read_anchors: Appendix A.1-A.5, especially evaluation and per-seed cost tables
records.mechanism: A score-aware LLM attributes agent credit across sampled topologies; credits guide offline pruning in a fixed supergraph.
records.boundary: Candidate evaluation counts are matched, not complete compute. Attribution costs are reported. Shared artifacts can mediate cooperation outside graph edges, so agent selection and communication are not fully separated.
records.implication_for_mab2: Credit-guided pruning alone is not new. Require graph-change-conditioned old-credit reuse, charged feedback acquisition and future service comparisons. No official implementation was verified in this lookup; absence of code is not claimed.
